name: Portuguese lessons
about: The path through the first Portuguese words, a few at a time, each in everyday sentences written for its lesson. Word list: FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, from OpenSubtitles (opensubtitles.org), CC BY-SA 4.0.

words.tomar: to drink, to have; to take
words.marcar: to book, to schedule; to mark
words.conhecer: to know, to be acquainted with
words.ficar: to stay; to be located; to become
words.saudade: longing; the feeling of missing someone or something
words.mandar: to send; to tell someone to do something
words.conseguir: to manage; to succeed; to get
words.segundo: second (time or position in order); according to
words.haver: to exist; used to express elapsed time
words.acompanhar: to follow; to keep up with
words.bater: to beat; to hit; to knock
words.nele: in him; in it; on it
words.nela: in her; in it; on it
words.aproveitar: to enjoy; to make the most of

oi.about: The everyday hello in Brazil, to anyone.

por-favor.about: Literally for favor: add it to any request.

obrigado.about: Literally obliged: a man says obrigado, a woman says obrigada.

tudo-bem.about: Literally all well? The everyday way to ask, and Tudo bem is the answer too.

o-que.about: Literally the what: the everyday way to start a question with what.

alguma-coisa.about: Literally some thing; in a question it can mean anything.

a-gente.about: Literally the people; everyday we, with the verb's ele form.

um-minuto.about: Literally one minute; in a request it can mean a moment.

hoje-a-noite.about: Literally today at night; à joins a and a.

la-fora.about: Literally there outside; normally just outside in English.

de-novo.about: Literally of new; the whole expression means again.

desculpa.about: A common casual apology; desculpe is also used.

em-frente.about: de combines with the following article: em frente da porta.

eu-a-conheco.about: a is the direct-object pronoun her here. This is common in careful speech and writing; conversational Brazil also uses conheço ela.

eu-o-conheco.about: o is the direct-object pronoun him here. This is common in careful speech and writing; conversational Brazil also uses conheço ele.

por-que.about: Two words when asking why before the rest of the question.

por-que-final.about: At the end of a question, quê carries an accent.

todo-mundo.about: Literally all world; the expression takes a third-person singular verb.

valeu.about: An informal Brazilian thank-you, used by a speaker of any gender.

as-vezes.about: Literally at the times; this expression describes something that happens on some occasions.

mesmo-assim.about: Introduces something true despite what has just been said.

por-isso.about: Refers back to the reason for what follows or precedes it.

na-verdade.about: Adds a fact that corrects or qualifies what was said or assumed.

pelo-menos.about: Sets a minimum or names something positive despite a problem: pelo menos eu liguei.

por-causa-do.about: por causa de introduces a reason; de + o joins as do.

a-partir-de.about: Introduces a starting point, including the date when a new arrangement begins.

para-tras.about: Gives the direction of a movement, as in um passo para trás.

words.means: comi = ate (with eu); comeu = ate (with você, ele, ela)
fiz = did, made (with eu); fez = did, made (with você, ele, ela)
vi = saw (with eu); viu = saw (with você, ele, ela)
li = read in the past (with eu); leu = read in the past (with você, ele, ela)

concept.line: Common verbs have their own completed-past forms: fiz/fez, vi/viu, li/leu. Learn the pair for eu and você; regular comer gives comi/comeu. No separate have is needed.

words.means: fui = went (with eu); foi = went (with você, ele, ela)
vim = came (with eu); veio = came (with você, ele, ela)
fiquei = stayed (with eu); ficou = stayed (with você, ele, ela)
cheguei = arrived (with eu); chegou = arrived (with você, ele, ela)
me (after a preposition, as in por mim)

concept.line: Movement also uses a single completed-past verb: fui/foi, vim/veio, cheguei/chegou. fiquei/ficou means stayed here.
nunca before the verb means never. In não li nada, nada follows a preverbal negative: I did not read anything. Portuguese negative words can reinforce the same negation.

words.means: pensar = think; penso = think (with eu); pensando = thinking (after estar); pensar em = think about
esses = these, those (with masculine plural nouns)
são = are (with vocês, eles, elas or plural things)
nesses = in these, in those (em + esses)

concept.line: Learn the verb with its complement: ajudar com, gostar de, pensar em, esperar por. esperar also takes a person directly: esperar você. These are patterns, not word-for-word English substitutions.
só can limit a request: só quero conversar means I only want to talk. um minuto can present it as brief. These words can soften a request, but tone and context still matter.
Describing words commonly follow the noun and agree with it: um bairro bonito, uma casa bonita. Other positions are possible; changing the order alone does not always make a mistake.

lessons.title: Taking a book to your brother
Asking someone to put a book here

words.means: pegar = pick up; pegue = pick up in a request
jogar = throw; jogue = throw in a request

concept.line: Use pegue, coloque and jogue for requests to você. Put não before the verb for a negative request: Não jogue esse livro. Other imperative forms also occur in everyday Brazilian speech.

words.means: parar = stop; pare = stop in a request
fechar = close; feche = close in a request
vir = come in its basic form
mesma = myself for a woman in eu mesma
quantos = how many with masculine plural nouns
essas = these, those with feminine plural nouns
os = the with masculine plural nouns
bonitas = beautiful with feminine plural nouns

concept.line: Many nouns add -s: livro/livros, foto/fotos. This path teaches full agreement: os livros, essas fotos bonitas. Spoken agreement varies.
A known noun can be left out: for books, tenho dois; for photos, quero uma. um/uma and dois/duas keep the gender of the understood noun. No extra word is required.
Use a plain infinitive in é seguro andar; para links tempo para comer; aprender takes a, and a hard thing is difícil de ler. A personal infinitive can name its own subject: para nós comermos.

lessons.title: Meeting someone for the first time

words.means: the time; primeira vez = first time
conheci/conheceu = met for the first time
primeira = first with a feminine noun
escrever = write; escrevo = I write; escreva = write in a request

concept.line: aprender takes a before an action: aprender a escrever. sem means without: sem ajuda, sem erros.

words.means: saudade = the feeling of missing someone or something
far away; longe de = far from
tomava = used to have or drink

concept.line: tomava describes a past habit: A gente às vezes tomava café junto. It does not present just one completed occasion.

words.means: the fear; ter medo = be afraid

concept.line: ter medo means be afraid: Eu tenho medo. estar com medo can describe feeling afraid now. Learn these expressions as wholes.
Learn confiar em and acreditar em: confio em você, acredito em você. Before o, em becomes no.
After quer, pode or vou, keep the infinitive organizar: Minha família quer organizar tudo.
não preciso says there is no need: Eu não preciso trabalhar hoje. It does not forbid working.

lessons.title: Keeping in touch during a busy week

words.means: falar = speak, talk; falo = I speak; fala = speaks
se = oneself; each other in these sentences
veem = see with eles, elas or vocês

concept.line: With people doing something to one another, se can mean each other: Eles se veem. In A gente se vê, the meaning can also be reciprocal even though a gente takes a singular verb.

words.means: the way; jeito de trabalhar = way of working
mudar = change; mudou = changed; mudando = changing
ficando = becoming or getting in these descriptions

concept.line: ficar with a description can express a change: O trabalho ficou diferente. está ficando describes a change in progress.

words.means: experimentar = try; experimente = try in a request

concept.line: gostar keeps de before what someone likes: gosto desse café. experimentar means try something, such as a new kind of coffee.
eu names the subject; mim can follow a preposition: para mim. In para eu fazer, eu is the subject of fazer. comigo means with me. a gente and nós both mean we, with their own verb forms.

words.means: sentir = feel; sinto = I feel; sente = feels

concept.line: With a description such as bem or forte, sentir takes me with eu and se with você or ela: Eu me sinto bem; ela se sente forte. With a noun such as dor or medo, or a body part, sentir takes no reflexive pronoun: Eu sinto dor no braço.

words.means: mandar = send; mando = I send; mande = send in a request
tiver = have in a future condition such as se você tiver

concept.line: For a possible future situation, use se tiver (if you have) or quando chegar (when you arrive). The main clause can make a request: Se você tiver tempo, mande a foto.

words.means: puxar = pull; puxe = pull in a request
solta = loose or free with a feminine noun
tive = had with eu; tive que = I had to

concept.line: Past forms can still take an infinitive: consegui abrir means managed to open; tive que puxar means had to pull. The first verb carries the past time.

words.means: deixar = let, leave; deixe = let or leave in a request
the moment; um momento = a moment
peace; em paz = in peace, alone

concept.line: um momento and por favor can make a request gentler: Deixe eu trabalhar em paz um momento, por favor. Tone and the situation still matter.

words.means: clara = clear with a feminine noun
trabalhado = worked, the participle used after ter

concept.line: tenho trabalhado describes repeated or continuing work over a recent period: Eu tenho trabalhado muito. For one completed event, Portuguese usually uses the simple past.

words.means: se = whether, introducing a yes-or-no question inside a sentence

concept.line: A question inside a sentence keeps its question word: Você sabe onde ela mora? Use se for whether: Eu não sei se ele vem. There is no English do or does to add.

words.means: like this; like that; this way

concept.line: Embedded questions also work with o que and como: Você sabe o que essa coisa faz? Você sabe como usar isso?

words.means: minutinho = a brief moment, a second in a request

concept.line: só can make a request sound limited, and um minutinho suggests a brief wait or favor. por favor adds please. These can soften a request; tone and context decide the effect.
ninguém means nobody. It can stand before the verb by itself, or follow não: Ninguém viu esse menino; não tem ninguém para ajudar.

words.means: elas = they, referring to women or feminine nouns

concept.line: deles and delas identify plural owners: o pai deles, a mãe delas. They follow the owners' gender and number, not the thing owned. seu/sua instead agree with the thing owned.

words.means: farei = I will do or make

concept.line: The simple future adds endings to an infinitive-based stem: ligarei, ficaremos. fazer has the irregular stem far-: farei. ir + infinitive remains the everyday choice for plans in speech.

words.means: esquecer = forget; esqueço = I forget; esqueci = I forgot; esquecido = forgotten
ligado = called, the participle after ter
feito = done or made, the participle after ter

concept.line: tenho + participle describes activity repeated or continuing over a recent period: tenho esquecido, tenho ligado, tenho feito. Use esqueci for one completed instance of forgetting.

words.means: próprio/própria = own, emphasizing the person something belongs to

concept.line: que links a person or thing to a describing clause: o livro que eu quero. onde links a place to what happens there: a cidade onde eu moro. English may omit that; these Portuguese examples keep que.

lessons.title: Supporting someone after losing a pet

words.means: cuidar de = take care of; cuido = I take care of
dias = days; todos os dias = every day
poderia = could, would be able to

concept.line: -ria forms can describe a hypothetical action or result: eu faria, seria. They can also soften a request: você poderia ajudar? Some stems are irregular, such as far- in faria. They do not replace every English would.

words.means: the reason; ter razão = be right
atrás = ago, after a length of time
era = was or used to be
morava = lived or used to live
tinha = had or used to have

concept.line: The imperfect gives past background or habits: antes eu morava aqui; quando eu cheguei, chovia. The simple past cheguei presents the arrival as a completed event. Duration alone does not determine which tense to use.

words.means: há = for, before an elapsed duration in these sentences
espero = I wait or am waiting

concept.line: For a situation continuing now, use the present or estar + gerund with há + a length of time: moro aqui há dois anos. faz + time + que also works: faz uma hora que espero. desde gives the starting point: desde segunda-feira.

words.means: possa = can or may in a subjunctive clause

concept.line: espero que introduces a hope with the subjunctive: espero que você venha, espero que o médico possa ajudar. venha and possa do not say the hoped-for event has already happened.

words.means: algum = some, a certain or unspecified one
querem = want, with eles, elas or vocês
cair = fall; cai = falls; caiu = fell
casar = get married; also used with me or se
agradeço = I thank; agradeço sua ajuda = I thank you for your help

concept.line: me and se can refer back to the subject in se casar: eu vou me casar, a gente vai se casar. English says get married. Brazilian speakers also say casar without the pronoun: a gente vai casar.

words.means: sair = leave, go out; saí = I left; saiu = left
chamar = call, name; chamam = call, with vocês, eles or elas
há = there is, there are in formal usage

concept.line: Everyday tem means there is or there are. More formal há does too: há espaço, há dois lugares. Both stay singular in this existential use. o senhor and a senhora take third-person singular verbs when addressing someone politely.

words.means: acalmei = I calmed; me acalmei = I calmed down
the evidence; a piece of evidence
passar = pass; passei = I passed; passou = passed

concept.line: estava + gerund describes what was going on at a past moment: eu estava fazendo café. Use estávamos with nós. A completed event can interrupt that background: quando você chegou.

words.means: baixo = quietly; mais baixo = more quietly
fale = speak; a request to você
acorde = wake up; subjunctive after antes que

concept.line: antes de takes an infinitive: antes de sair, antes de a gente sair. With antes que, use the subjunctive: antes que o bebê acorde.

words.means: fazermos = for us to do or make; personal infinitive with nós
sairmos = for us to leave; personal infinitive with nós

concept.line: An infinitive can have its own subject: para eu fazer, antes de a gente sair. With nós it can take -mos: para nós fazermos. eu and a gente use the unchanged form.

words.means: the condition; em bom estado = in good condition
estiver = be; future subjunctive with a singular subject
puder = can; future subjunctive with a singular subject
quiser = want; future subjunctive with a singular subject

concept.line: Use the future subjunctive for a future event after quando or a future condition after se: quando você chegar, se eu puder. The clause can come first or last; the main clause keeps ordinary word order.

words.means: lembro = I remember; lembra = remember with você; lembrar-se de names what is remembered

concept.line: In lembrar-se de, the pronoun refers to the subject: eu me lembro, você se lembra. de introduces what is remembered. Brazilian speakers also say eu lembro de, without the pronoun.

lessons.title: Get a photo the right way up

words.means: pendurada = hanging, describing a feminine noun
virar = turn; vire = turn, a request to você
nessa = in that, in this; em + essa

lessons.title: Get help with a difficult text

concept.line: que links a person or thing to a clause: a parte que você precisa ler, a pessoa que pode ajudar. It stays que regardless of gender or number. Keep the preposition when the verb requires it: a pessoa de quem eu me lembro.

words.means: né = right?; an informal check for agreement

concept.line: An infinitive clause can name who acts: é normal o bebê dormir, para você descansar. eu, você, ele, ela and a gente use the unchanged infinitive form.

há uma hora que ela está dormindo means she has been sleeping for an hour. The same duration can follow the action: ela está dormindo há uma hora. sentado and deitado describe posture and agree with the person.

words.means: consigo = I can, I manage to; consegue = can, manages to with você
sumir = disappear; some = disappears; sumiu = disappeared
tinham = had; imperfect with eles, elas or vocês

concept.line: tinha + past participle says what had happened before another past moment: quando eu cheguei, ele já tinha saído. Use tinham with eles, elas or vocês. The participle stays unchanged after ter.

words.means: falar sério = be serious, mean it
fosse = were; imperfect subjunctive in como se fosse
estivesse = were; imperfect subjunctive in como se estivesse
soubesse = knew; imperfect subjunctive in como se soubesse

concept.line: como se introduces an imagined comparison with the imperfect subjunctive: como se fosse, como se estivesse, como se soubesse. Here these forms need not describe past time; they mean as if a situation were true.

words.means: minhas = my, with feminine plural nouns

concept.line: consegui and tive que describe a completed past event here: consegui carregar means managed to carry; tive que carregar means had to carry. Keep the following action in the infinitive.

words.means: pude = I was able to; podia = could, used to be able to

concept.line: In a completed past event, consegui means managed to, pude means was able to, and tive que means had to. The next verb stays in the infinitive. podia and tinha que describe past ability or obligation as background or habit.

words.means: tanto = so much, describing an action here
possamos = can, present subjunctive with nós; poder = be able to

concept.line: A hope or desired result can use que + subjunctive: espero que você venha, quero que você brinque, para que nós possamos brincar. A scheduled expectation can instead use espero você às cinco.

words.means: Deus = God, capitalized as a name
the right; a right to do something
vendida = sold; vende-se = for sale on a sign; vendendo = selling

concept.line: ser + a past participle says what is done to something: A casa foi vendida. The participle agrees with that thing. está sendo feita describes an action in progress. Vende-se casa is a sign; in conversation, Estão vendendo a casa is more natural.

lessons.title: A film that stays with you

words.means: bater = beat, hit, knock; bate = beats; batendo = beating

concept.line: Use mais ... do que, menos ... do que, and tão ... quanto to compare: mais bonita do que, menos bonito do que, tão grande quanto. maior means bigger; menor means smaller. The shorter que can also introduce a comparison.

words.means: bata = hit or knock, a você command; batendo = hitting, knocking, beating
conduzir = lead, as in lead a meeting
better; o melhor or a melhor = the best

concept.line: melhor means better; o melhor or a melhor identifies the best. Use o/a mais ... de for the most ... in a group: a casa mais bonita do bairro. The article agrees with the noun, even when that noun is understood.

words.means: concordo = I agree; concordar com alguém = agree with someone
the point; a detail in a discussion
de + isso: of that, about that
em + isso: in that, about that

concept.line: Referring back still keeps the preposition: falar disso means talk about that; pensar nisso means think about that. disso is de + isso, and nisso is em + isso.

lessons.title: What do you think of it?

words.means: em + ele: in him, in it, about it after pensar
pensa = thinks; with você, you think
dessa = de + essa, of this or that feminine thing
em + ela: in her, in it, on it

concept.line: Keep the preposition when referring back: falar disso (talk about that), pensar nisso (think about that), gostar dele (like him or it). disso joins de + isso; nisso joins em + isso. dele and dela can refer to people or to masculine and feminine things.

words.means: ando = I walk; ande = walk, a request to você
sensible; a sensible thing to do

concept.line: poderia can suggest a possibility or soften a request. seria sensato + infinitive suggests a sensible action: Seria sensato esperar. The linked action stays in the infinitive.

words.means: suas = your, his, or her, with feminine plural nouns
me arrependo = I regret; se arrepende = you regret

concept.line: In eu me sinto and você se arrepende, the pronoun points back to the subject. arrepender-se de names what someone regrets. eu mesmo becomes eu mesma for a woman.
me in eu me sinto and se in você se sente point back to the person feeling something. ficar can describe a change or a stay: fiquei doente, fiquei no hospital.

words.means: me acalmar = calm down, with eu understood
droga! = damn it!; an informal exclamation of frustration

concept.line: ficar + bravo/brava describes becoming angry: eu fico bravo, você fica brava. Choose bravo or brava for the person described; the verb keeps its subject ending.

words.means: acalmo = I calm; me acalmo = I calm down

concept.line: me in eu me acalmo refers back to eu: I calm down. ficar brava describes becoming angry, while estar bravo describes being angry.

words.means: leve = take, a request to você
traga = bring, a request to você; trouxe = I brought or brought with você, ele, ela

concept.line: Leve um casaco asks someone to take a jacket; Traga isso para mim asks them to bring it to the speaker. para can introduce a recipient or destination, while por can give the reason: por causa do frio. These are whole verbs, levar and trazer.

lessons.title: What do you feel like doing?

words.means: the desire; estar com vontade de = feel like doing
prefere = prefers; with você, you prefer

concept.line: gostar keeps de before the activity: gosto de rir, gostaria de ficar. gostaria de expresses would like. estar com vontade de describes what someone feels like doing now.
Questions keep ordinary clause order. Quanto asks about an amount; quantos asks about a masculine plural count. um pouco de introduces a small amount.

words.means: the guest; convidada = a woman guest; convidados = guests
quantas = how many, with feminine plural nouns

concept.line: Quantas pessoas counts people; quantos convidados counts guests. A question with quem asks who someone is. Ordinal segundo/segunda agrees with the noun it describes.

words.means: todo = every, in em todo lugar (everywhere)
colocou = put, with você, ele or ela in the completed past
procura = looks for, with você, ele or ela

concept.line: Onde asks where something is. em todo lugar means everywhere. In está procurando, estar carries the subject and tense while procurando names the ongoing search.

words.means: publicar = publish; publicada = published, feminine singular
lê = reads, with você, ele or ela

concept.line: foi publicada presents a completed action done to the news item. era conhecida describes its earlier known status with the imperfect. Passive participles and descriptive adjectives agree with the noun.

words.means: the partner; parceira = a woman partner

concept.line: nosso and nossa agree with what belongs to us: nosso carro, nossa casa. Everyday a gente means we and takes a third-person singular verb, as in a gente comprou.

words.means: vão = go, with eles, elas or vocês
servir = fit; serve = fits, for clothing here
uso = I wear or use; usa = wears or uses

concept.line: Color adjectives follow the noun here: casaco preto, xícara preta. They agree with that noun. Compare sizes with maior or menor: esse tamanho é maior.

words.means: the prison; na prisão = in prison
trabalhava = worked or used to work

concept.line: que connects a noun to a clause identifying it: o advogado que trabalha aqui, o homem que está na prisão. The clause has its own subject and verb.

words.means: the silence; em silêncio = quietly, in silence

concept.line: A reflexive pronoun can refer back to the subject: eu me acalmo, ela se viu. lembrar-se de names what someone remembers. Brazilian speakers also use lembrar de without the pronoun.

words.means: the card; a greeting card here
escolhe = chooses, with você, ele or ela
the contact; contato com = contact with
toda = every, with a feminine singular noun

concept.line: me and te can name the recipient of a message: ela me manda uma mensagem. A reference after a preposition keeps it: com ela, com isso. isso can refer back to a thing or situation.

words.means: passado/passada = last, previous, after a time word
descobrir = find out, discover; descobri = I found out

concept.line: Use the imperfect for past background or habits, such as estava de folga and morava aqui. The simple past presents completed events: comprei, descobri. A time expression alone does not choose the tense.
gostaria de can introduce a wish gently, while poderia can soften a request. seria describes a hypothetical result or assessment. These forms do not replace every English would.

words.means: gritar = shout; gritando = shouting; grite = shout in a você request

concept.line: A negative request can use não + grite: Não grite. parar de links to an infinitive: pare de gritar. por favor softens a request; tone still matters.

words.means: verificar = check; verifique = check in a você request
estejam = be, present subjunctive with eles, elas or vocês

concept.line: espero que can introduce a hope with the present subjunctive: espero que todos estejam bem. A future possibility after se or quando uses the future subjunctive: se tiver perigo, quando você chegar.

words.means: decidir = decide; decida = decide, present subjunctive or a você request

concept.line: For a future event, use quando você decidir. A desired outcome after espero que or quero que uses the present subjunctive: espero que o presidente decida, quero que você decida.
Use the imperfect for past background: o rei era jovem. The simple past presents a completed event: eu vi o rei.

words.means: correr = run; corro = I run; corra = run in a request

concept.line: corra, pegue and jogue can ask one person to act: Corra para cá. This path uses these você request forms; other spoken Brazilian forms are also common.
por can mark a route, para a destination, and de a starting point: pela rua, para casa, do escritório. pela joins por + a; do joins de + o.

lessons.title: Where does that plane come from?

concept.line: de can name where something comes from, and para where it is going. de + o becomes do; em + o becomes no: do país, no avião.
para can mark the destination and por the route: para o hotel, pelo bairro. no hotel joins em + o for a location.

words.means: mexer = move; mexa = move in a request
tente = try in a request; tento = I try
a second, a unit of time
volta = comes back or goes back

lessons.title: A short visit to your uncle

concept.line: às sete means at seven. The time of an event can use ser: a consulta é às sete. To say how long something lasts, use a duration such as por pouco tempo.

words.means: meia = half, with a feminine noun such as hora

concept.line: São duas e meia means it is two thirty. meia stands for meia hora, half an hour, even in meio-dia e meia. Quinze para as três means a quarter to three. Use é with uma or meio-dia, and são with plural hours.

lessons.title: Coffee and a book on a bench

words.means: cafezinho = a coffee, said warmly or often a small serving

concept.line: -inho and -inha can suggest smallness, affection or a gentler request: uma casinha, um cafezinho, um minutinho. The noun keeps its gender. Endings and spelling vary: café becomes cafezinho.

words.means: cantar = sing; canto = I sing; canta = sings; cante = sing in a request
aproveitar = enjoy or make the most of; aproveite = enjoy in a request

concept.line: comigo means with me; conosco means with us. These are prepositional pronouns: cantar comigo, cantar conosco. Everyday com a gente is also common.

words.means: nas = in the or on the, with feminine plural nouns
nessas = in these or about these, with feminine plural nouns

concept.line: Keep the expression's preposition when referring back: pensar nisso means think about that, and falar disso means talk about that. nisso joins em + isso; disso joins de + isso.
exceto eu means except me: eu identifies the person left out. segundo ela means according to her, while para mim means for me. Learn the pronoun with its role and expression.

words.means: estive = I was, for a completed period
teve = had, for a completed event or period

concept.line: The simple past presents an event or period as a whole: estive no hospital, tive um dia bom. The imperfect gives background: estava com dor. estar com dor means be in pain; eu me senti describes how I felt.

words.means: escapar = escape; escapou = escaped; escapado = past participle
perdoar = forgive; perdoo = I forgive; perdoei = I forgave

concept.line: tinha + participle places an action before another past moment: quando a polícia chegou, ele já tinha escapado. The participle stays unchanged after ter. me and te identify the person forgiven in me perdoar and te perdoei.

words.means: chorar = cry; chorando = crying; chorei = I cried

concept.line: A hope after espero que can use the present subjunctive: espero que você possa descansar. possa is the singular present subjunctive of poder, followed by an infinitive: possa descansar, possa oferecer ajuda.

lessons.title: An animal rescue in the news

words.means: pular = jump; pulou = jumped; pule = jump in a request
us; ourselves or each other when referring back to nós
contei = I told; contou = told; contamos = we tell or we told
dessas = of these or of those, with feminine plural nouns

concept.line: In eu me sinto and a gente se lembra, the pronoun points back to the subject. nos can mean us as an object, or each other in nós nos contamos histórias. Everyday a gente takes a singular verb: a gente se lembra.
